summary: Surface plot of the [Bose-Einstein distribution](../particle-statistics) over the complex plane. This plot shows an important feature of the [Matsubara formalism](../matsubara-contours) developed for QFT at non-zero temperature. It's a method to calculate expectation values of operators in a canonical ensemble evolved by an imaginary time. In momentum space, this leads to the replacement of continuous frequencies by discrete imaginary (Matsubara) frequencies. Away from the imaginary axis, the distribution becomes approximately flat, particularly at sufficiently low temperatures. Pulled from [arxiv:1712.09863](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09863).

summary: Reproduced from [Bartel (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10853-022-06915-4). The convex hull of stability represents the lowest energy surface in composition space for a given chemical system. It is constructed by connecting the energies of the most thermodynamically stable compounds at each composition. For visual clarity, only ground-state phases at each composition are shown. Legend: - Blue circles: Stable phases lying on the convex hull (blue line) - Red squares: Unstable phases above the hull - Orange dashed line: Chemical potential range where AX is stable - ΔE_d: Decomposition enthalpy, the energy above the hull for unstable phases Materials on the hull are stable against decomposition into other phases. The energy difference between a material and the hull (hull distance) quantifies its thermodynamic stability - larger distances meaning less stable and harder to synthesize, making the convex hull a powerful tool for guiding experimental synthesis efforts.
title: Convex Hull of Stability

summary: Three ordered rotations describe the orientation of a frame in 3D. This diagram uses the intrinsic Z–Y–Z convention: precession $\psi$ about the original $z$ axis, nutation $\theta$ about the intermediate $v$ axis, and spin $\varphi$ about the tilted $z_1$ axis. Blue, orange, and teal distinguish the three stages; the final basis is $(x_1,y_1,z_1)$. Reordering the rotations generally changes the final orientation. A single external leg meets a vertex from which a [propagator](../qft-propagators) loop carrying momentum $q$ closes back on itself, cut open by the regulator insertion (circled cross). This tadpole is the simplest non-trivial diagram in the [functional renormalization group](../rg-flow-in-theory-space) hierarchy.

summary: This [Feynman diagram](../feynman-building-blocks) corresponds to the integrand in this expression for $$ \displaystyle \partial_t \Gamma_{k,a}^{(1)}(q) = -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{\substack{i,j\\k,l}}^N \int_{\substack{p_1,p_2\\p_3^\prime,p_4^\prime}} \frac{\partial_t R_{k,ij}(p_1,p_2)}{\Gamma_{k,jk}^{(2)}(p_2,p_3) + R_{k,jk}(p_2,p_3)} \, \frac{\Gamma_{k,akl}^{(3)}(q,p_3,p_4)}{\Gamma_{k,li}^{(2)}(p_4,p_1) + R_{k,li}(p_4,p_1)}. $$

summary: This Feynman diagram contains two [propagators](../qft-propagators) forming a loop carrying the external energy $q_0$. $m_{1,2}$ denote the masses of the propagators and $\gamma_{1,2}$ their decay width which, for an expansion in Minkowski space, are non-zero only around a real and positive on-shell frequency $p_0 > 0$.
title: Feynman Diagram Propagator Loop

summary: Two Feynman diagrams showing [loop corrections](../propagator-fluctuations) to a propagator. Each diagram contains a loop with momentum q₀ and two external lines with coupling g. The loops include mass terms m₁², m₂² and width terms γ₁², γ₂². The diagrams differ in the position of the [regulator insertion](../regulated-and-unregulated-propagators) (cross marker) which appears at the bottom vertex in the first diagram and at the top in the second.
title: Feynman Diagrams Loop Regulator

summary: Exercise illustration: Compute the pressure of an ideal gas in three dimensions upon a wall at $x = 0$ that attracts molecules at large distance and repels them at smaller distance. Let the force be given by the potential $U(x) = -A \, e^{-\alpha x} + B \, e^{-2 \alpha x}$, with $A,B > 0$.
title: Gas Pressure on Wall

summary: [Generative adversarial network (GAN)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2661) architecture. A GAN has two parts. The discriminator $D$ acts as a classifier that learns to distinguish fake data produced by the generator $G$ from real data. $G$ incurs a penalty when $D$ detects implausible results. This signal is backpropagated through the generator weights such that $G$ learns to produce more realistic samples over time, eventually fooling the discriminator if training succeeds.
title: Generative Adversarial Network

summary: Bayes' theorem as an argument about areas. The square is the whole probability space, split horizontally by the prior $p(H)$ against $p(\neg H)$ and vertically by the likelihoods, so each of the four rectangles is a joint probability. Conditioning on the evidence $E$ keeps only the two rectangles where $E$ occurred; rescaling those to full height renormalizes them into the posterior $p(H|E)$ shown on the right. Following [3blue1brown](https://youtu.be/HZGCoVF3YvM).
title: Geometric Bayes

summary: Graphs can look differently but be identical. The only thing that matters are which nodes are connected to which other nodes. If there exists an edge-preserving bijection between two graphs, in other words if there exists a function that maps nodes from one graph onto those of another such that the set of connections for each node remain identical, the two graph are said to be [isomorphic](https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/algorithms/isomorphism.html).

Unlike other fundamental forces, graviton self-interactions lead to infinitely many terms of increasing complexity, resulting in the non-renormalizability of gravity and motivating the need for theories like string theory.

summary: The $k$-space region of wave vectors up to a given magnitude is a disk of area $\pi k^2$. The $k$-space area occupied by a single particle state is $$ \frac{1}{2} \frac{2 \pi}{L_x} \frac{2 \pi}{L_y} = \frac{2 \pi^2}{A}, $$ where the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ is due to the spin degeneracy $g_s = 2 s + 1 = 2$. The number of states with wave vector magnitude smaller than $k$ is $$ N(k) = \frac{\pi k^2}{2 \pi^2/A} = \frac{A k^2}{2 \pi}. $$ $k$-space is used extensively in solid state physics e.g. to visualize the [energy bands](../how-atoms-become-energy-bands) of a material as a function of electron momentum. In position space, the position-energy dispersion would just be a probability blur.
title: k-Space

summary: One of the pivotal insights of the 2nd superstring revolution point was [Edward Witten's formulation of M-Theory in 1995](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9503124). Before that, there had been 5 different types of string theories, each 10-dimensional: Type I, Type IIa and IIb, and two different heterotic theories. Witten showed that all of these theories are simply different limiting cases of a single overarching string theory (without showing what that underlying theory actually is). See Sean [Carroll's excellent post](https://preposterousuniverse.com/blog/2014/03/12) on M-Theory for details.

summary: Building a [torus](../torus) by declaring the plane periodic. Once translation by $2\pi$ in either direction is a symmetry, a single lattice cell already carries every point: it is a fundamental domain. Gluing that cell's horizontal edges $b$ rolls it into a cylinder, and gluing the two rims $a$ that are left closes the cylinder into a torus. The chevrons track the orientation each edge is glued with, since reversing one instead yields a Klein bottle. The two edge pairs survive the construction as the torus's two independent loops, the generators of $\pi_1(T^2) = \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$, which are what a closed string winds around in a compactified dimension.
title: Plane to Torus

summary: Parallel-plate capacitor filled with a dielectric. The free charge $\pm Q_\text{C}$ on the plates drives the field $\vec E$, which lines the molecular dipoles up with it. Alignment leaves uncompensated bound charge $\mp Q_\text{surf}$ on the two faces of the dielectric, pointing against the free charge, so the net field is weaker and the capacitance higher than in vacuum.
title: Plate Capacitor

summary: The three one-loop diagrams contributing to the flow of the two-point function. The first two place the [regulator](../regulated-and-unregulated-propagators) insertion $\partial_k R_k$ above and below a loop closed by two dressed three-point vertices $\Gamma_k^3$; the third is a [tadpole](../feynman-diagram-loop) carrying a single four-point vertex $\Gamma_k^4$. Their sum is the right-hand side of the flow equation for the inverse propagator, and the regulator is what makes each momentum integral converge.
title: Propagator Fluctuations

summary: Complex plane visualization of propagator poles and [branch cuts](../branch-cuts-1) in quantum field theory. The diagram shows the analytic structure of Green's functions, including the relationship between retarded/advanced propagators and the placement of poles relative to the real axis. This structure helps understand causality and the connection to [Matsubara frequencies](../matsubara-contours).
title: QFT Propagator Poles

summary: Complex plane visualization of different propagator types in quantum field theory: retarded, advanced, and Feynman propagators. The diagram shows their [analytic structure](../qft-propagator-poles) in relation to [Matsubara frequencies](../matsubara-contours) (dots on imaginary axis). This representation helps understanding causality in quantum field theory and the connection between real-time and imaginary-time (thermal) formalisms.
title: QFT Propagators

summary: Diagram of the random forest (RF) algorithm ([Breiman 2001](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~breiman/randomforest2001.pdf)). RFs are ensembles model consisting of binary decision trees that predicts the mode of individual tree predictions in classification or the mean in regression. Every node in a decision tree is a condition on a single feature, chosen to split the dataset into two so that similar samples end up in the same set. RFs are inspectable, invariant to scaling and other feature transformations, robust to inclusion of irrelevant features and can estimate feature importance via mean decrease in impurity (MDI).
title: Random Forest

summary: Comparison between [regular neural networks](../multilayer-perceptron) and [Bayesian neural networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05424). The diagram illustrates how Bayesian networks incorporate uncertainty in their predictions by treating weights as probability distributions rather than point values, leading to more robust predictions with uncertainty estimates.
title: Regular vs Bayes NN

summary: A grid-world policy that [greedily selects](https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262039246/reinforcement-learning/) the locally best action under estimated state values, steering toward the goal while avoiding a penalty state.

summary: Visualization of [renormalization group (RG) flow](../wetterich-equation) trajectories in the theory space of all possible coupling constants (λ₁, λ₂, λ₃, λ₄) allowed by symmetries. The diagram shows how different microscopic actions (S₁, S₂, S₃) obey the same symmetries and thus flow to the same quantum effective action (Γ) through different paths, each corresponding to a different choice of infrared regulator R_k(q). This illustrates the universality of the effective action despite different starting points and regulators.
title: RG Flow in Theory Space

Intermediate binding balances these competing requirements. summary: [Attention as a weighted sum](../single-head-attention) over a set. Each input embedding $\vec e_i$ is scored against the query $\vec e_j$ by the attention function $a_\varphi$, giving the weight $\alpha_{ij}$, while $f_\psi$ maps the same input to the value being weighted. Multiplying and summing over $i$ yields the updated embedding $\vec e_j'$. The sum is permutation-invariant, which is why the mechanism applies to unordered sets as readily as to sequences. From [arxiv:1706.03762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762).

summary: Classical elastic scattering of [light](../light) by a free electron. The incident electric field drives the electron's oscillation, and the accelerated charge reradiates. A highlighted outgoing wave defines the scattering angle $\theta$ relative to the forward direction. Incident and scattered waves have the same wavelength and photon energy in the Thomson limit $h\nu \ll m_e c^2$, where recoil is neglected. The gray rays indicate other possible emission directions schematically.
title: Thomson Scattering

summary: A torus is obtained by [identifying matching opposite edges](../plane-to-torus) of a lattice's fundamental cell. The blue and teal arrows show the two pairs of identified edges. The map $z \mapsto z/u$ rotates and uniformly scales both lattice generators, taking $2\pi u$ to $2\pi$ and $2\pi v$ to $2\pi\tau$, where $\tau = v/u$ and $\operatorname{Im}\tau > 0$. The two panels have the same conformal shape; the normalized lattice makes its [complex parameter](../torus-fundamental-domain) explicit.
title: Tori

summary: Three-dimensional visualization of a torus with major radius R and minor radius r. The torus is a fundamental geometric object in string theory, where strings can wrap around its [two independent cycles](../plane-to-torus). Its topology allows for periodic boundary conditions in two directions, which is relevant when studying compactification, [modular invariance](../torus-fundamental-domain), and dualities in string theory.
title: Torus

summary: The light gray-shaded areas show a fundamental domain of a torus under modular transformations. The diagram shows the region in the complex plane that uniquely parametrizes [inequivalent tori](../tori), bounded by the modular projective special linear group PSL(2,Z) transformations that identify physically equivalent fundamental domains for the action of $\Gamma$ on the upper half-plane.

summary: The Wetterich eqn. is a non-linear functional integro-differential equation of one-loop structure that determines the scale-dependence of the flowing action $\Gamma_k$ in terms of fluctuations of the [fully-dressed regularized propagator](../regulated-and-unregulated-propagators) $[\Gamma_k^{(2)} + R_k]^{-1}$. It admits a simple [diagrammatic representation](../feynman-building-blocks) as a one-loop equation as shown in this diagram.
